title: Structured bedside handoff checklist and missed medication reconciliation items on an acute medical ward
subtitle: QI project with PDSA cycles and run charts, Ward 6B
statement: On Ward 6B, nursing shift handoff is verbal and held at the nurses' station, and the medicines content depends on what the outgoing nurse recalls. A local check of 60 handoff sheets against the medication administration record found 23 (38 percent) with at least one missed reconciliation item, and two near misses in August involved doses stopped on the day shift and given again at night. The project will test whether a structured bedside handoff checklist with a short medicines section reduces the proportion of handoffs with a missed reconciliation item.
whoAffected: Adult inpatients on Ward 6B (32 beds, mostly older adults with several regular medicines), the registered nurses handing over and receiving care, and the ward pharmacist who resolves discrepancies on the morning round.
whatHurts: Held doses, new high-alert medicines and same-day prescription changes are not passed on reliably, so a dose can be repeated, omitted or given against a changed plan. Patients and families rarely hear what changed, and night nurses spend time reconstructing the day's decisions from the record.
currentPractice: Verbal handoff at the nurses' station at 07:00 and 19:00 using a free-text handoff sheet with no medicines prompt. Reconciliation discrepancies are found by the ward pharmacist on the morning round, usually after at least one dose has been affected.
whyNow: Two near misses in August, a local baseline showing 38 percent of handoffs missing at least one reconciliation item, and a nurse manager willing to protect huddle time for improvement work this autumn.
constraints: No research funding; work happens within normal shifts; the checklist must take under two minutes per patient on nights; no electronic record changes before 2027; the research ethics office screened the work as quality improvement (QIS-2026-118).
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient on Ward 6B receives the right doses across the shift change, and patients who are awake know what changed in their medicines today.
summary: Problem framed as a ward-level QI project: reduce missed medication reconciliation items at nursing handoff with a structured bedside checklist tested in PDSA cycles.
